about: What each engine mod needs of the model and the command before its switch changes anything, read from the mod's own engage condition in its patch (arkey_ie_mods 2c72325; ec06fea for the mods past the pin sparse-split, idx-keys, topk-rowhist, kpool-mask-range, ple-prefetch-step, ple-prefetch-prompt; 18351f1 for kv-stream, whose gate changed at ad16a8c, and concat-rows; evidence: the patch file and its line). slots (a row's server slots its code needs, with slots_why): the command's slots must be that count (-np; the shape's slots), and session-ab and load-probe refuse a command that sets the switch without it. workflow/mods.shape_why reads it, for a switch, a knob row of the mod's group, a spend row and a memory row alike: tune sets a built mod's switch only when `needs` holds over the shape the model's header and the command show (tune_llama_cpp.model_shape: indexer, pool_ratio, top_k, key_length, value_length, head_count, head_count_kv, experts, host_experts, recurrent, per_layer_embedding, draft, kv_type, arch), and says why when it does not. off_shape: what the mod does off its shape (silent: nothing, with no word; logged; refuses; n/a). arch appears only where the mod's own code gates on the architecture's name: a limit of that mod, recorded as such, never a BoltBeam key. A mod with no row is not set, said: adding a mod adds its row (tests/test_machine_figures.py fails when a mod of the pinned index, or of the index past the pin kept in tests/data/ie_mods_past_pin.json, has none). Not expressible in these facts, so not checked: a sliding-window model's checkpoints, a k-pool read from another header key, the draft's kind and its own expert count, whether the expert cache is on.

Also needed, not in these facts: one KV stream on the GPU

chip_status.about: Where each mod was built, checked and measured, per chip: BoltBeam's stand-in until arkey_ie_mods carries the row itself. The schema is the mods repo's to adopt: an index mod row's `chips` ({chip: {level, evidence}}) is that mod's one authoritative row and, when present, is read in place of these (workflow/mods.chip_status); until then a version row here grants a level on a chip to the mods it names, as of the index commit the evidence was taken at (at): a mod it does not name, with no row of its own, has no level there (refused, said: no evidence is recorded), never the version's. chip: the GPU architecture the build compiles for (sm_120, gfx1201: a target's compiler_arch, workflow/mods.chip_of). level, rising: builds < checked < measured (levels_why). A mod is applied on a chip at `applies` or above; a mod at builds is refused there by default and applied only with --allow-build-only, said in the plan, every row and the build record; a chip with no row is refused, said. A row never borrows across chips.

levels_why.builds: the mod's patch applies and the engine compiles for this chip; nothing has run on it
levels_why.checked: its check mode passed on this chip (its output against stock, the arkey_ie_mods check switch)
levels_why.measured: checked, and its speed measured on this chip against stock
